- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.10), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect market resilience.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the first 5–7 days of the 30d horizon; apply a 2–5% upward bias for early periods.
- After sharp price spikes (≥ 5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon; if forecast is > 20% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10%.
- Sentiment volatility > 0.20 in last 5 days correlates with forecast error; apply smoothing filter to reduce noise in 30d forecast.
- If sentiment history shows repeated positive spikes followed by negative sentiment, model tends to “forget” the spike; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% after 2–3 negative sentiment days.
